guide.title: Toxicology & Overdose
guide.lead: You rarely know the drug, but the body tells you the class. Read the pupils, skin, temperature and breathing. Support the airway and breathing first, then the antidote. Some poisons look harmless for hours, so bring the containers and transport.

sections.title: Toxidromes
rows: Salivation, bronchorrhea, vomiting, diarrhea, slow pulse

steps.title: Airway and BVM first
steps.text: Ventilate with oxygen before any drug.

steps.title: Aim for breathing
steps.text: Not full wakefulness: abrupt withdrawal brings vomiting and agitation.

steps.title: Transport
steps.text: Naloxone can wear off before the opioid.

sections.title: Specific poisons
rows: Headache, nausea, several people or pets ill; SpO₂ falsely normal
Seizures, low BP, QRS wider than 100 ms
Looks well, then bradycardia and shock
Cool; benzodiazepines (ALS); avoid struggling against restraint

sections.title: Every poisoning
items: Bring all containers and pills; note the time
Activated charcoal 50 g within 1 hour only with a protected airway and per protocol
Alcohol withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium tremens: benzodiazepines (ALS)

quiz.q: Unresponsive, breathing 6/min, pinpoint pupils. First intervention?
options: Open the airway and ventilate with a BVM, then naloxone

quiz.q: A family has headache, nausea and confusion; the furnace runs nonstop; SpO₂ 98% on all. Cause?
options: Carbon monoxide: SpO₂ is falsely normal; 100% oxygen
quiz.explanation: Several people ill in one building is a clue.

quiz.q: Amitriptyline overdose with seizures and a wide-complex tachycardia. Explanation?
options: Tricyclic sodium-channel blockade: wide QRS, seizures, arrest risk
quiz.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate (ALS) for QRS wider than 100 ms.

quiz.q: Big pupils, hot dry red skin, delirium and urinary retention:
quiz.explanation: "Hot as a hare, dry as a bone, red as a beet, mad as a hatter."

quiz.q: Pinpoint pupils, drooling, wheeze with secretions, vomiting and a slow pulse after spraying crops:

options: No oxygen if SpO₂ is normal

quiz.q: A beta-blocker overdose patient feels fine. Plan?
options: Transport and monitor: they can crash suddenly
Within 1 hour of a toxic ingestion with a protected airway, per protocol
For every overdose at any time
When the patient is drowsy and can't protect the airway

flashcards.question: Opioid overdose triad
flashcards.answer: Respiratory depression, reduced consciousness, pinpoint pupils.

flashcards.question: Naloxone doses
flashcards.answer: 0.4 mg IV/IM, titrated and repeated every 2–3 minutes; or 4 mg intranasal spray. Ventilate first.

flashcards.question: Why transport after naloxone?
flashcards.answer: Naloxone can wear off before the opioid: breathing can fail again.

flashcards.question: Delirium tremens
flashcards.answer: Severe alcohol withdrawal: confusion, fever, tachycardia, high BP, hallucinations, seizures. Benzodiazepines (ALS).

flashcards.question: Stimulant overdose
flashcards.answer: Agitation, hypertension, tachycardia, hyperthermia, big pupils, sweating; risk of seizures, MI, stroke. Cool, benzodiazepines, avoid struggling against restraint.

flashcards.question: Tricyclic overdose ECG
flashcards.answer: QRS wider than 100 ms from sodium-channel blockade: seizures and arrest risk. Sodium bicarbonate (ALS).

flashcards.question: Carbon monoxide and pulse oximetry
flashcards.answer: Standard oximeters read carboxyhemoglobin as oxygen: SpO₂ is falsely normal. 100% oxygen at 15 L/min.

flashcards.question: Toxidrome: big pupils, hot dry red skin, delirium

critical.scenario: A 24-year-old with a history of heroin use: RR 4 and shallow, SpO₂ 80%, HR 62, pupils 1 mm, no response to pain. A syringe on the nightstand.
critical.question: Sequence of interventions?

options.t: Open the airway, ventilate with a BVM and oxygen, then naloxone (0.4 mg IV/IM titrated or 4 mg intranasal) while ventilating
Naloxone first, ventilate only if it fails

critical.explanation: Transport even if he wakes: naloxone can wear off first.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes airway and ventilation before medication administration in opioid overdose

critical.scenario: A 22-year-old took cocaine 30 minutes ago: agitated, confused, hot (39.6 °C), BP 180/104, HR 138, big pupils. Friends are holding him down on the bed.
critical.question: How do you manage him?

options.t: Police for safety, clear the room, de-escalate, cool him, avoid prolonged struggling against restraint, ALS sedation per protocol, rapid transport
Let the friends hold him down harder
options.f: Struggling raises heat and acidosis; risk of sudden death.

options.t: Lie him prone to control him
Leave him to sleep it off

critical.explanation: Severe sympathomimetic toxicity: cooling and benzodiazepines are the treatment.
critical.kpi: Recognizes the dangers of physical restraint in hyperthermic stimulant overdose

critical.scenario: A 45-year-old took an unknown number of her husband's heart pills 90 minutes ago. She felt fine; now she's drowsy and HR has dropped to 58. Bottles: metoprolol, lisinopril, amiodarone.
critical.question: Concern and action?

options.t: Beta-blocker toxicity developing: frequent vital signs, monitor and 12-lead, contact medical direction or the poison centre, rapid transport with the bottles

options.f: Drowsiness and falling HR are toxicity.

critical.explanation: Cardiac drug overdoses can look well before sudden bradycardia and shock.
critical.kpi: Recognizes delayed toxicity in polypharmacy overdose despite initial normal vital signs
